_v1_notes.CAPTOR|LOCATION: a lone disturbed individual is N for a moving vehicle, a remote compound and an undisclosed location - none is achievable without planning or organisation. A state security service is N for a city building or a vehicle: it detains in its own facilities.
_v1_notes.CAPTOR|RESOLUTION METHOD: ransom is N for an ideological cell (no money motive) and N for a lone individual (no coherent demand to pay). A state service admits negotiation only - assault on a sovereign facility is not an option, nor is ransom.
_v1_notes.CAPTOR|INTELLIGENCE AVAILABLE: a lone individual x communications intercept is N: no organisation communicating. A state service x live internal imagery is N: penetrating a state detention facility with live sensors is not on the table.
_v1_notes.CAPTOR|TIME PRESSURE: a lone individual is N at months - no endurance. A state service is N at immediate threat to life: its whole method is indefinite detention.
_v1_notes.LOCATION|RESOLUTION METHOD: a moving vehicle is N for deliberate assault - there is no static target to rehearse against. An undisclosed location is N for both assault types: nothing to assault.
_v1_notes.LOCATION|INTELLIGENCE AVAILABLE: a moving vehicle is N for live internal imagery. An undisclosed location is N for imagery and N for 'nothing beyond location', since the location is precisely what is not known.
_v1_notes.LOCATION|TIME PRESSURE: a moving vehicle is N at days and months - transit does not continue that long.
_v1_notes.RESOLUTION METHOD|INTELLIGENCE AVAILABLE: deliberate assault is N on communications intercept alone and N on nothing-but-location: neither gives interior positions to plan against. Emergency assault is N on intercept alone.
_v1_notes.RESOLUTION METHOD|TIME PRESSURE: negotiation, deliberate assault and ransom are all N under immediate threat to life - none fits in minutes. Emergency assault is N at days and months, being definitionally a response to an immediate threat.
